prompt: The team holds back 20% of the data that the model never sees during training, then scores it there.
why: Scoring on data the model never saw in training shows how it will do on new cases. Holding data back for that is a train/test split.
trap: It's the check, not the problem it catches.

prompt: Like a student who practices on old exams but is graded on a new one, the model is scored on fresh examples.
why: Being graded on unseen questions shows real understanding. Scoring a model on examples it never trained on is what a test set is for.
trap: Memorizing is the risk; the new exam is the split.

prompt: Accuracy is reported only on examples kept aside from training.
why: Reporting accuracy only on examples kept out of training gives an honest score. Those kept-aside examples are the test set.

prompt: Before training, the data is split so there's a fair final check.
tells: split so there's a fair final check
why: Splitting before training keeps some data untouched for a fair final check. That's a train/test split.
trap: Splitting is the safeguard against leakage, not leakage.

prompt: To check the model honestly, it's tested on customers from a later month than it trained on.
tells: a later month than it trained on
why: Testing on a later month than training mimics using the model on the future. A split by time is an honest train/test split.
trap: Using later data for testing prevents leakage.

prompt: The data is cut into a training part and a testing part.
tells: a training part and a testing part
why: One part is for learning and the other for checking. Cutting the data that way is the train/test split.
